newsitem.title: USA: Case against Malcolm X's daughter comes to end.
newsitem.headline: Case against Malcolm X's daughter comes to end.

text.p: Federal prosecutors have closed the books on a murder-for-hire case involving Malcolm X's daughter and Nation of Islam leader Louis Farrakhan, her assassinated father's rival.

Judge James Rosenbaum of the U.S. District signed an order Thursday dismissing a 1995 indictment against Qubilah Bahiyah Shabazz after prosecutors said she had successfully completed a two-year probationary period, the U.S. Attorney's office in Minneapolis said.
She was indicted in January 1995 on charges that she tried to hire a man she had known since high school to kill Farrakhan, her father's bitter enemy before his assassination more than 30 years ago.

The government agreed on May 1, 1995, to drop the charges in the alleged Farrakhan plot if Shabazz underwent a trouble-free two-year probation that included psychiatric, drug and alcohol abuse counselling.
Shabazz, 36, has been living in Texas where she works for a radio station.
Shabazz's lawyers contended she was entrapped by her friend, Michael Fitzpatrick, who was a government informant, and she later said she was only joking when she mentioned killing Farrakhan.

Shabazz's family over the years has said they believed Farrakhan had a role in the death of the firebrand black separatist who was gunned down in 1965 -- something that Farrakhan has vehemently denied.
